arxiv-2105-06809.title: The double copy: from optics to quantum gravity Journal: osajournal Publication type: Tutorial
arxiv-2105-06809.creator: Chris D. White, \authormark 1
arxiv-2105-06809.description: Abstract Recently, an intriguing relationship (the double copy ) has been discovered between theories like electromagnetism, and gravity. This potentially gives us a new way to think about gravity, and there are also practical applications involving the efficient calculation of gravitational observables, and also how to simulate gravity using optical systems.

arxiv-2112-12857.title: Variational quantum circuits to prepare low energy symmetry states
arxiv-2112-12857.creator: Raja Selvarajan, Manas Sajjan, Sabre Kais
arxiv-2112-12857.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Raja Selvarajan, Manas Sajjan, Sabre Kais. We explore how to build quantum circuits that compute the lowest energy state corresponding to a given Hamiltonian within a Symmetry subspace by explicitly encoding it into the circuit. We create an explicit unitary and a variationally trained unitary that maps any vector output by ansatz A ⁡ ( α → ) A(\vec{\alpha}) from a defined subspace to a vector in the symmetry space.

arxiv-2309-03826.title: Gænice: a general model for magnon band structure of artificial spin ices
arxiv-2309-03826.creator: Ghanem Alatteili, Victoria Martinez, Alison Roxburgh, Jack C. Gartside, Olle G. Heinonen, Sebastian Gliga, Ezio Iacocca
arxiv-2309-03826.description: Abstract Arrays of artificial spin ices exhibit reconfigurable ferromagnetic resonance frequencies that can be leveraged and designed for potential applications. However, analytical and numerical studies of the frequency response of artificial spin ices have remained somewhat limited due to the need of take into account nonlocal dipole fields in theoretical calculations or by long computation times in micromagnetic simulations.

arxiv-2501-02225.title: Tracking Star-Forming Cores as Mass Reservoirs in Clustered and Isolated Regions Using Numerical Passive Tracer Particles
arxiv-2501-02225.creator: Shingo Nozaki, Hajime Fukushima, Kazuki Tokuda, Masahiro N. Machida
arxiv-2501-02225.description: Abstract Understanding the physical properties of star-forming cores as mass reservoirs for protostars, and the impact of turbulence, is crucial in star formation studies. We implemented passive tracer particles in clump-scale numerical simulations with turbulence strengths of ℳ rms = 2 , 10 \mathcal{M}_{\rm rms}=2,10 .

arxiv-2504-04921.title: Expectations vs Reality - A Secondary Study on AI Adoption in Software Testing
arxiv-2504-04921.creator: Katja Karhu, Jussi Kasurinen, Kari Smolander
arxiv-2504-04921.description: Abstract In the software industry, artificial intelligence (AI) has been utilized more and more in software development activities. In some activities, such as coding, AI has already been an everyday tool, but in software testing activities AI it has not yet made a significant breakthrough.

pmc-10710245.title: Development and Validation of a Routine Session-by-Session Experience Measure for Youth Mental Health Services: My Youth Mental Health Session Experience (MySE)
pmc-10710245.creator: Debra J Rickwood, Sabina Albrecht, Nic Telford
pmc-10710245.description: PurposeThe ‘My youth mental health Session Experience’ (MySE) measure was developed by headspace, Australia’s National Youth Mental Health Foundation, in collaboration with young people, for use as a routine session experience measure across its national centre service network. pmc-11671116.title: Persistence of Uterine Artery Doppler Velocimetry Changes in Postpartum Mothers Following a Delivery Complicated by Preeclampsia: A Systematic Review
pmc-11671116.creator: Prathamesh Lanjewar, Sivaranjani P Selvam, Avir Sarkar, Shivam Pandey
pmc-11671116.description: In preeclampsia, there occurs a defective trophoblastic invasion of spiral arteries, which is characterized by abnormal uterine artery wave parameter such as increased pulsatility index (PI) and early diastolic notch. This increased uterine artery PI is a good predictor of hypertensive disorder and small for gestational-age babies. Maternal hypertension and proteinuria resolve in the puerperium.

pmc-12596140.title: ZeroGEN: leveraging language models for zero-shot ligand design from protein sequences
pmc-12596140.creator: Yangyang Chen, Zixu Wang, Pengyong Li, Li Zeng, Xiangxiang Zeng, Lei Xu, Xin Gao
pmc-12596140.description: MotivationDeep generative methods based on language models have the capability to generate new data that resemble a given distribution and have begun to gain traction in ligand design. However, existing models face significant challenges when it comes to generating ligands for unseen targets, a scenario known as zero-shot learning.

pmc-12620221.title: Trends and comparative analysis of the burden of migraine in China and globally from 1990 to 2021: an analysis based on the 2021 global burden of disease study
pmc-12620221.creator: Bo Peng, Yuluo Tu, Suifa Hu, Gui Xie
pmc-12620221.description: BackgroundMigraine is a common neurological disorder that has become an increasingly significant public health issue. This study aims to analyze the burden of migraine in China and globally from 1990 to 2021, exploring epidemiological trends and differences, thus providing scientific evidence for migraine prevention and control.

pmc-12637203.title: Patient administrative burden: a scoping review
pmc-12637203.creator: Michael Anne Kyle, Kimberly Y Feng, Carrie G Wade, Miranda Yaver
pmc-12637203.description: IntroductionHigh administrative costs are a notable feature and frustration of the American health care system. Administrative complexity drives excess health care spending and clinician burnout. There is growing interest in patient administrative burden: the nonclinical, administrative work a patient must do to use the health care system.

pmc-13421690.title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of Rhynchium brunneum (Fabricius, 1793) (Hymenoptera: Vespidae)
pmc-13421690.creator: Jing Wang, Shulin He, Bin Chen, Tingjing Li
pmc-13421690.description: The wasps of Rhynchium exemplify solitary vespid predators controlling Lepidopteran pests through venom-mediated paralysis, with their venom possessing significant medicinal potential. As dominant models within the species-rich subfamily Eumeninae representing 70% of Vespidae diversity, they provide critical insights into sociality evolution and biocontrol mechanisms.

Whoever, acting or claiming to act in any office or capacity under the United States, or a State, without lawful authority grants, issues, or verifies any passport or other instrument in the nature of a passport to or for any.
